summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, aortic valve replacement, and chronic venous insufficiency was admitted for fever, worsening shortness of breath, and increased erythema and pain in her left lower extremity. She had recently been switched from Keflex to minocycline for infection suppression but developed fever and clinical deterioration. IV vancomycin was initiated, and she was transitioned to oral linezolid after blood and urine cultures showed no significant growth. Her heart failure was stable, though her BNP was elevated; torsemide was reduced to 80 mg daily. She improved clinically, with resolving fever and leg inflammation, and was discharged home on a two-week course of linezolid, with instructions for leg compression, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up care.
